description: Helps you decide what sellers should say at each stage of a deal, from your product, the persona you sell to and your proof points. Optional objections, value propositions, competitor objections, price context, sales stage and business model shape it. Returns a pitch order, an answer to each objection with the proof point that fits it, competitor responses, discovery questions and follow up templates. Without objections it suggests the ones your sector raises. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of email_sequence_generator when you need seller messaging, objection responses and discovery prompts.

business_model.description: Optional: how you charge, so the advice fits it. If omitted, it is read from your text and the answer says how. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "saas".

common_objections.description: Optional: sales objections you hear, one per line, per semicolon or comma-separated. If not provided, likely objections for your sector are suggested. Format is text. For example, "The reviewer asked who owns unresolved exceptions.".

competitor_objections.description: Optional: 'why not [competitor]' objections. Format is text. For example, "The reviewer asked who owns unresolved exceptions.".

price_context.description: Optional: your pricing against the market (for example 'Premium, above market', 'Budget option' or 'Mid-market'). Format is text.

product.description: The product name and what it does. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

proof_points.description: Evidence for your claims: case studies, metrics and quotes, one per line, per semicolon or comma-separated. Format is text. For example, "Company-reported pilot reduced approval time from 12 to 9 days in October 2026.".

sales_stage.description: The stage of the sales funnel. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "prospecting".

target_persona.description: Who sales is pitching to (role and company type). Format is text. For example, "finance director".

value_props.description: Optional: key value propositions, one per line, per semicolon or comma-separated. Taken from the proof points if not provided. Format is text. For example, "resolve invoice exceptions before month-end".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".
